caption: Matthew gives Jesus’s enemies almost the exact taunt from Psalm 22. It is exceptionally close literary reuse—not independent evidence of a forecast.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 22 predict this exact taunt? Mockers tell the psalmist to trust God for rescue. Matthew gives almost the same words to Jesus’s enemies.
slides.body: Mockers tell the psalmist to trust God for rescue. Matthew gives almost the same words to Jesus’s enemies.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 22 predict this exact taunt?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 22:8: He trusts in the LORD, let the LORD deliver him.
slides.body: He trusts in the LORD, let the LORD deliver him.
slides.heading: Ps 22:8

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Matt 27:43, BSB: He trusts in God. Let God deliver Him now if He wants Him. For He said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”
slides.body: He trusts in God. Let God deliver Him now if He wants Him. For He said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Matt 27:43

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The connection is exceptionally close It appears among several Psalm 22 echoes. Matthew deliberately casts Jesus as the mocked righteous sufferer.
slides.body: It appears among several Psalm 22 echoes. Matthew deliberately casts Jesus as the mocked righteous sufferer.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But Matthew uses the psalm’s words The psalm records an existing taunt. The match clearly shows literary reuse, whatever happened historically.
